_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war LIVE — Section 338 50% tariffs operative since Aug 22; Canada 893-line retaliation effective Sept 8 (9 days); talks suspended; Trump 50% auto tariff threat Jan 1 2027
themes.summary: As of August 30, the Canada-US trade war remains at maximum escalation with the next hard catalyst — Canada's September 8 retaliatory tariff effective date — now nine days away. The US Section 338 50% tariffs on approximately $27.6 billion of Canadian goods have been fully operative since August 22. Canada's Department of Finance confirmed on August 25 the official 893-tariff-line retaliation list covering $27.6 billion in annual US imports, with rates of 15%, 25%, and 50% matched precisely to the equivalent US Section 338 and Section 232 rates. Targeted sectors include steel and aluminum (existing counter-tariffs rising from 25% to 50% to match US rates), dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics, and electronics. The September 8 effective date stands firm and there is no active diplomatic channel: Prime Minister Carney confirmed negotiations remain suspended, having recalled Canada's negotiating team after the US proposed terms Canada characterized as asking 'too much' and offering 'too little.' Trump has separately threatened to raise tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel to 50% on January 1, 2027, adding a structural medium-term CAD negative beyond the current Sept 8 catalyst. USDCAD traded near 1.3882–1.3895 in the Aug 27 session before the Warsh hawkish surprise at Jackson Hole on Aug 28 added additional USD support — USDCAD is now in the 1.39 area, probing the topside with the dual tailwind of CAD structural weakness from tariff shock and a re-strengthening USD from the post-Warsh hawkish repricing. The key binary on September 8 remains whether the US counter-retaliates against Canada's measures (USTR Greer had previously flagged willingness to respond) or absorbs them without immediate escalation. Canada's $7.5 billion worker and business support package, announced alongside the retaliation list, signals Ottawa is prepared for a prolonged dispute rather than a quick resolution. Section 338 carries no statutory expiry. USMCA formal review with Canada has not commenced and escalating conflict makes near-term resumption unlikely.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM CAD negative — US 50% tariffs live since Aug 22, full retaliation list published Aug 25 with Sept 8 effective date, negotiations explicitly suspended, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat adds structural overhang. USDCAD ~1.39, approaching key 1.3900 level. BoC rate hike expectations further compressed as tariff growth drag dominates. Sept 8 is the next hard catalyst: US counter-retaliation (consistent with Greer's prior signalling) = USDCAD accelerates above 1.40; US silence/absorption = modest near-term CAD relief but structural weakness remains. Dual tariff shock (US 50% on CAD goods + CAD 15-50% retaliation raising input costs for Canadian industry) amplifies growth damage beyond the direct export hit.
implications.USD: USDCAD directionally bullish from tariff shock, now reinforced by post-Warsh hawkish USD repricing. DXY ~99.68 (Aug 29), up 0.89% on the week. Canada tariff shock adds modest USD safe-haven bid vs commodity bloc.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated on the US-Mexico track, though Mexico-specific tariff track advancing separately. Modest USDMXN risk premium from contagion.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc contagion — AUD trades defensively in acute CAD-shock episodes. AUDUSD has partially retraced multi-month highs on post-Warsh USD strength; vulnerable to further risk-off from US-Canada escalation spiral post Sept 8.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path and post-Warsh USD dynamics.
implications.JPY: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus structural JPY bid from BOJ Sep hike cycle.

Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: BOJ Sep 17-18 hike ~80% priced + intervention regime — Tokyo CPI core-core hit 2.0% Aug 28; Reuters: BOJ may hike faster than twice-yearly pace; USDJPY touched 160 Aug 29 on Warsh USD surge; Takata Sep 2 next catalyst
themes.summary: As of August 30, USDJPY briefly touched the critical 160.00 level during overseas trading on August 29, driven by the post-Warsh hawkish USD repricing that added 12bps to the US 2yr yield (to 4.352%, highest since July 24). The BOJ Sep hike narrative remains firmly intact after a strong Tokyo CPI print on August 28: headline CPI rose 1.9% YoY in August (from 1.8% in July), core CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.8% YoY beating the 1.7% consensus forecast, and crucially the core-core gauge (excluding fresh food and energy, the BOJ's preferred underlying measure) accelerated from 1.8% to 2.0% YoY — hitting the BOJ's 2% inflation target directly for the first time in this cycle. The composition shows persistent domestic price pressure: food prices up 3.9% YoY, eating out up 5.0%, housing up 1.9%. Additionally, wholesale inflation spiked to 7.2% YoY in July, reflecting Middle East-related cost pressures working through the pricing chain with a lag. Reuters sources confirmed the BOJ is set to hike as soon as September and is considering a more aggressive pace of tightening than its recent roughly twice-yearly cadence. BOJ Deputy Governor Himino had set up the print on August 27, saying underlying inflation was 'approaching 2 percent' and reiterating that the BOJ should continue raising rates in a timely manner. The BOJ raised rates to 1.00% in June (a 31-year high), held in July, but issued its strongest comments yet on mounting inflation risk. Market pricing for a September 17-18 move to 1.25% sits near 80%, having pulled back modestly from 86% pre-Warsh as the USD rate differential repriced higher. The next BOJ calendar events are: Takata speech September 2 (Takata dissented at the July meeting in favour of raising rates immediately to 1.25%), Masu speech September 10, and Ueda's press briefing after the G20 gathering. The joint US-Japan intervention regime, established at end-July when a ~$59 billion operation drove USDJPY to 155.27, has not been tested in over four weeks. The USDJPY 160.00 touch on August 29 is now an acute stress test of the regime's credibility — the question is whether MoF will verbally intervene or act ahead of the September 17-18 BOJ meeting given that a hike at that meeting would itself provide fundamental JPY support.

implications.JPY: Three-pillar structural JPY support in tension with post-Warsh USD strength: (1) Intervention regime — dry powder preserved, credibility tested by 160 touch on Aug 29; (2) BOJ Sep hike ~80% priced, Tokyo core-core at 2.0% cements hike case, Reuters sources confirm; (3) Fed rate differential narrowing from BOJ side even as Warsh hawkish repricing partially restores USD yield support. Net: intervention threat and Sep 17-18 BOJ hike binary still dominate medium-term USDJPY direction lower; post-Warsh USD strength adds near-term upside pressure. 160.00 is now the live line in the sand for MoF/BOJ coordination.
implications.USD: USDJPY topside meets intervention threat at 160; post-Warsh hawkish repricing (Sep hike odds 57.5%, DXY ~99.68) is now the dominant near-term USD driver across pairs. Rate differential direction of travel remains USD-negative vs JPY from both sides over medium term but short-term USD support restored.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under pressure from intervention mechanism and BOJ hike pricing. EURUSD dynamics primarily driven by Warsh/Fed repricing now — ECB hawkishness noted but rate differential still favours EUR over USD medium-term.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure. GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY lower on intervention pressure. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ hike cycle.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention pressure. AUDUSD partially reversed multi-month highs on post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention pressure; NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on post-Warsh USD strength.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is now the LIVE critical line — briefly touched Aug 29, which is the clearest stress test of the intervention regime in four weeks. A daily close above 160 without MoF verbal or actual intervention signals carry traders have overpowered the regime. MoF/BOJ verbal intervention threshold: expect strongly-worded warnings from Kato or MoF if USDJPY sustains above 160 in Tokyo hours. USDJPY below 158.00 = intervention credibility reasserting after 160 touch. USDJPY below 155.27 (post-intervention low) = regime decisively winning. Takata speech Sep 2: Takata is the most hawkish board member (dissented for immediate hike in July) — any explicit Sep hike endorsement = renewed JPY bid, USDJPY pressured toward 157-158. Masu speech Sep 10 is the final BOJ pre-meeting communication. Ueda G20 press briefing: any explicit guidance is an additional catalyst. BOJ Sep 17-18 is the hard binary: hike to 1.25% = USDJPY likely drops toward 155-152; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 160+ re-test, intervention regime faces acute stress. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately.

themes.title: Warsh hawkish at Jackson Hole Aug 28 — Sep hike odds surged to 57.5%, DXY ~99.68, 2yr yield 4.352%; next hard events: Sep 11 CPI (August) and Sep 16 FOMC with SEP/dots
themes.summary: As of August 30, the Jackson Hole binary has resolved decisively hawkish. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's August 28 keynote — his first as Fed Chair and his 100th day in the role — delivered a clearer inflation-fighting signal than the market's 69% consensus for a neutral tone had anticipated. Warsh stated that inflation 'remains higher than the central bank's longstanding goal of 2%' and suggested the Fed 'may need to raise interest rates in the coming months.' He acknowledged that 'while this summer's [inflation] readings were better than expected, they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.' Warsh doubled down on his refusal to provide forward guidance ('I stand here today committed to a discipline, not to a decision'), saying the Fed should not 'indulge a regime in which market participants are looking primarily to the Fed for their next trade.' While he stopped short of explicitly pre-committing to a September hike, the remarks were interpreted as hawkish given they came against a 69% neutral expectation and alongside the July PCE beat (headline 3.7% YoY, above 3.6% consensus). The market reaction was sharp: September FOMC hike odds jumped from approximately 35% pre-speech to 57.5% post-speech; the US 2-year Treasury yield rose 11.97bps in a single day to 4.352%, its highest since July 24; DXY closed at approximately 99.68 on August 29, up 0.89% on the week; USDJPY briefly touched 160.00; gold fell over $100/oz; Bitcoin fell below $80,000. The move is consistent with the broader Warsh regime narrative: he replaced Powell in late May, sowed confusion at his July 29 press conference, and the Jackson Hole speech has now provided the first unambiguous signal that his threshold for hiking is lower than markets had priced in the 69%-neutral baseline. The next hard policy event is the September 16 FOMC with updated SEP and dot plot — the real tiebreaker for 2026 rate path. The critical pre-FOMC data event is September 11 CPI (August data). A Chicago PMI downside surprise (47.1 vs 57.9 expected) on August 28 created a counterpoint — deteriorating business sentiment and tightening signals within the same 24 hours — but did not materially dent the hike repricing. Year-end hike odds remain elevated.

implications.USD: DXY ~99.68, up on the week post-Warsh hawkish surprise. Sep hike odds at 57.5%, a majority for the first time in this cycle. The repricing adds a new structural USD bid that was absent in the prior 'neutral/framework' expectation regime. Near-term path depends on: Sep 11 August CPI (hot = cements Sep hike, DXY toward 100.50+; soft = hike odds pull back toward 45%, DXY retraces), Sep 16 FOMC dots (2026 dot at 4.0%+ = full hawkish validation; dots unchanged = sell-the-news USD weakness). DXY sustaining above 100.00 = hawkish repricing fully priced; DXY failing back below 98.50 = markets unwinding Warsh hawkish read.
implications.JPY: Warsh hawkish outcome partially restores rate differential, creating cross-current against BOJ Sep hike narrative. USDJPY touched 160.00 Aug 29 — the intervention regime's credibility is now being tested in real time. Net: post-Warsh USD support is a USDJPY upside force, BOJ Sep hike + intervention regime is a USDJPY downside force; balance shifts from day to day based on MoF signalling and incoming data.
implications.EUR: EURUSD likely retraced from 1.1657 toward 1.1500-1.1550 on Warsh hawkish repricing. ECB hawkishness (eurozone inflation signs) provides partial offset but rate differential still moved against EUR on the week. Sep 11 US CPI and Sep 16 FOMC are the next major EURUSD catalysts.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength. BoE at 3.75% vs Fed now with majority expecting a hike to 3.75-4.00% — rate convergence story has partially shifted back in USD's favour. BoE's own path and August UK data remain independent GBP drivers.
implications.CAD: Post-Warsh USD strength adds a second tailwind to USDCAD alongside the Section 338 tariff shock. USDCAD probing 1.39. BoC rate expectations already compressed; any Warsh-induced growth concern (Chicago PMI 47.1) adds risk-off pressure on CAD.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD partially reversed multi-month highs on Warsh hawkish USD repricing. China demand dynamics and RBA path are independent AUD drivers. Dual headwind from stronger USD and commodity-bloc risk-off.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on Warsh USD bid.
implications.CHF: USDCHF lifted by Warsh hawkish repricing. SNB easing mode limits CHF upside. CHF safe-haven bid provides partial offset in risk-off episodes.

themes.watchLevel: Sep 11 August CPI is the next critical data event: hot print (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = Sep hike fully priced above 70%, DXY targets 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350-1.1450; soft print (core at or below 0.2% MoM) = hike odds pull back toward 45-50%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary: hike 25bps to 3.75-4.00% = full hawkish validation, DXY toward 101-102, EURUSD below 1.1300; hold with hawkish dots (2026 median above 4.00%) = partial validation, DXY 100-101; hold with unchanged dots = sell-the-news USD weakness, DXY retraces toward 98. DXY sustaining above 100.50 = full hawkish repricing underway. DXY closing and sustaining below 98.00 = Warsh hawkish read fully unwound. USDJPY 160.00 is the intervention tripwire — if MoF acts between now and Sep 16, JPY gains dominate regardless of USD direction. Chicago PMI downside miss (47.1) on Aug 28 is a growth caution — if ISM Manufacturing and payrolls (Sep 4) show similar deterioration, stagflation narrative limits how far rate hike pricing can extend.
